newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says goodbye to Uncle Buddy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says goodbye to Uncle Buddy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton made a sombre tour of his boyhood hometown on Thursday, visiting his mother's grave and attending a funeral for the great-uncle who influenced his earliest years.

After leaving a bouquet of fresh flowers at the grave of his mother, Virginia Kelley, at Rose Hill Cemetery, Clinton addressed mourners at the funeral of Henry Oren Grisham, who died on Monday at age 92. Clinton knew him as "Uncle Buddy."
Speaking at the funeral chapel, Clinton remembered his great uncle as being both "brutally honest and always kind."
Clinton said he had always felt at home with Uncle Buddy "when I was a young boy badly in need of a hand up and a little kindness and wisdom."

The Rev. I.V. Hight said he went to see Grisham after Clinton was elected president and Grisham said he was not happy at Clinton's election. Hight said Grisham told him: "I'm afraid they will kill him."
"He viewed Bill as the boy that he loved," Hight said.

During Clinton's 1992 run for the presidency, Clinton called Grisham "a real important part of my early life." Clinton never knew his own father, William Blythe, who died three months before he was born.
Grisham was a steady presence during Clinton's formative years, especially during the time that Clinton lived with his maternal grandparents while his mother was training to be a nurse-anaesthetist.
Born on Dec. 11, 1904, near Hope, Grisham worked as a firefighter at a military ordinance plant in Texas and later owned a pastry shop in Hope.
